title: AQ Podcast | Daniel Noboa’s Ecuador: Crime, Protests and a Contested Vote
author: NOVEMBER 12, 2026
text:
FacebookXLinkedInThreadsEmailShare

Reading Time: < 1 minute

Ecuador is facing one of the most consequential moments in its recent history. President Daniel Noboa won reelection in April 2025 on a promise to restore public security, but despite an increasingly aggressive campaign against organized crime and closer ties with the United States, the country continues to struggle with entrenched criminal networks. Homicides are down about 8% this year after a record-setting 2025, and Noboa is increasingly compared to El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele. Now, local elections on November 29 will test Noboa’s political strength, with the main opposition party barred from running under its own name, and one of its top leaders in jail. Our guest is Sebastián Hurtado, co-founder and CEO of Prófitas, a political risk consultancy based in Quito.

Guest:

Sebastián Hurtado is founder and president of PRóFITAS, a leading political risk consultancy based in Quito.

Host:

Jose Enrique Arrioja, Managing Editor of Americas Quarterly
